examples.en: My heart pounded before the presentation.
I trembled with a racing heart waiting for the results.
It was my first date, so my heart fluttered.
I was nervous with a pounding heart before opening the letter.

examples.ko: 놀이기구를 타기 전부터 심장이 두근두근 뛰어요.
examples.en: My heart starts thumping even before I get on the ride.
I opened the gift with excited anticipation.

explain: 설레거나 긴장할 때 심장이 뛰는 소리와 느낌을 흉내 내는 말이에요. 좋은 기대와 불안 둘 다에 쓰고, '두근거리다'와 '두근두근하다'는 같은 느낌의 동사예요. '쿵쾅쿵쾅'은 더 세게 뛸 때 써요.
explain_en: It imitates the sound and feeling of a heartbeat when you are excited or nervous, and works for both happy anticipation and anxiety. 두근거리다 and 두근두근하다 are verbs with the same feel. 쿵쾅쿵쾅 is for a much harder pounding.

examples.en: The blanket dried in the sun is really soft and dry.

examples.ko: 샤워 후에 뽀송뽀송한 수건으로 닦으니 기분이 좋아요.
examples.en: Wiping off with a dry, fluffy towel after a shower feels good.

examples.ko: 빨래가 뽀송뽀송해지려면 바람이 잘 통해야 해요.
examples.en: For laundry to dry nicely, the air needs to circulate well.
I want to keep my room dry even in the rainy season.
Applying powder makes my face feel smooth and dry, and I like that.

examples.ko: 건조기에서 갓 나온 옷은 늘 뽀송뽀송하네요.
examples.en: Clothes fresh out of the dryer are always nice and dry.

explain: 축축하지 않고 산뜻하게 마르면서 부드러운 느낌일 때 써요. 이불, 수건, 빨래, 피부에 자주 쓰고 반대말은 '눅눅하다, 축축하다'예요.
explain_en: It is used when something is not damp but fresh, dry and soft. It often describes blankets, towels, laundry and skin, and the opposites are '눅눅하다' and '축축하다'.

examples.en: I twisted my ankle coming down the stairs.
If you sprain something while exercising, apply ice right away.
My foot twisted and I almost fell.

examples.ko: 손목을 삐끗한 것 같아서 병원에 갔어요.
examples.en: I thought I had sprained my wrist, so I went to the hospital.
Go down carefully so you don't twist anything.
I may have wrenched it, because my lower back keeps hurting.

explain: '삐다, 접질리다'와 비슷하지만 '삐끗하다'는 관절이 순간적으로 살짝 어긋난 느낌이에요. 몸뿐 아니라 '계획이 삐끗하다'처럼 일이 조금 어긋날 때도 써요.
explain_en: It is similar to '삐다' and '접질리다', but '삐끗하다' gives the feel of a joint slipping slightly out of place for a moment. It is also used for things going slightly wrong, as in '계획이 삐끗하다'.

examples.en: I pulled up my pants and started walking again.

examples.ko: 그는 눈썹을 추켜올리며 놀란 표정을 지었어요.
examples.en: He raised his eyebrows and looked surprised.

examples.ko: 무거운 가방을 어깨 위로 추켜올리는 모습이 힘들어 보였어요.
examples.en: Hitching the heavy bag up onto his shoulder looked tiring.
My skirt keeps slipping down, so I keep having to pull it up.

examples.ko: 안경을 코 위로 추켜올리면 잘 보여요.
examples.en: If I push my glasses up my nose, I can see well.
The jeans were too big, so I was busy pulling them up all the time.

explain: 바지, 양말, 안경, 눈썹, 어깨처럼 몸에 붙은 것을 위로 쭉 올릴 때 잘 써요. 반대로 아래로 내릴 때는 '내리다'를 써요. '추켜올려요', '추켜올렸어요'처럼 바뀌어서 어간이 달라지는 점에 주의해요.
explain_en: It's used when you pull something attached to the body upward, such as pants, socks, glasses, eyebrows or shoulders. For lowering something, you use '내리다'. Note that it changes form to '추켜올려요' and '추켜올렸어요', so the stem shape changes.

examples.en: I changed into a patient gown at the hospital.

examples.ko: 환자복을 입으니 진짜 환자가 된 것 같았어요.
examples.en: Putting on the hospital gown made me feel like a real patient.
I put a cardigan over my hospital gown and went for a walk.
When I was discharged, I returned the hospital gown to the nurse.
The hospital gown was big, so I had to roll up the sleeves.

examples.ko: 환자복 차림으로 복도를 걷는 사람이 많았어요.
examples.en: Many people were walking down the hall in hospital gowns.

explain: 입원했을 때 병원에서 주는 옷이에요. '환자복을 입다/갈아입다/벗다'처럼 말하고, 집에서 입는 잠옷이나 운동복과는 달라요.
explain_en: This is the clothing the hospital gives you when you are admitted. You say '환자복을 입다/갈아입다/벗다', and it is different from pajamas or sportswear worn at home.

en: scar; fault (talked about behind someone's back)

examples.en: A small scar was left where I got hurt.

examples.ko: 남의 흉을 보는 건 나쁜 버릇이에요.
examples.en: Badmouthing other people is a bad habit.

examples.ko: 그 흉은 시간이 지나면 거의 안 보일 거예요.
examples.en: That scar will hardly be visible after some time.

examples.ko: 친구 앞에서 남의 흉만 보면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't do nothing but badmouth others in front of your friends.
Everybody has a flaw or two.

examples.ko: 수술 자국이 흉으로 남아서 신경 쓰여요.
examples.en: The surgery mark stayed as a scar, and it bothers me.

explain: '흉'은 몸에 남은 상처 자국도, 남의 부족한 점도 가리켜요. 몸의 자국은 '흉터'라고 하는 경우가 훨씬 많아요. '흉을 보다'는 없는 자리에서 남의 단점을 말하는 거라 조심해서 써야 해요.

phrases.example: 그 사람이 없을 때 모두 흉을 봤어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 자리에 없는 사람의 단점을 말하는 거예요. 줄여서 '흉보다'라고도 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means talking about the faults of someone who isn't there. It can be shortened to '흉보다'.

explain_en: '흉' can mean a mark left on the body or a fault in someone else. For a mark on the body, '흉터' is used much more often. '흉을 보다' means talking about someone's faults when they are not there, so use it carefully.
